verdicts.rationale: Pure MLP/SGD/batch-norm/dropout/L1-L2 background on Fashion-MNIST. Appendix E (PyTorch mini-book) and Ch 0 (DL essentials) already cover these primitives. Nothing LLM- or VLM-specific.
Convolution, pooling, strides, padding, receptive fields, MobileNet. Pre-ViT CNN background. Ch 22 (VLMs) operates at ViT/CLIP/DINOv2 layer, not convolutional primitives. No enrichment value.

Transfer learning recipe, VGG16, ResNet residual connections, facial keypoint regression, multi-task age/gender. Residual connection idea is already a basic Transformer building block; nothing new for a VLM/LLM book.
Grad-CAM, data augmentation, batch-norm ablation, imbalanced data tips. Interpretability for CNN classifiers; the book's interpretability chapters focus on attention/probing for LLMs. Out of scope.

Adversarial image attacks on CNNs and neural style transfer via Gram matrices. Adversarial robustness exists in the book at the prompt/LLM jailbreak level; image-pixel adversaries on VGG16 are out of scope.

Selective search, Felzenszwalb, IoU, NMS, mAP, R-CNN, Fast R-CNN with PyTorch implementations. Ch 22.1 and 22.3 already cite Faster R-CNN and the R-CNN region-feature lineage at the conceptual level needed for VLMs (LXMERT/ViLBERT context). Browser agents in Ch 29 use DOM/accessibility trees, not bounding boxes. Two-stage detector internals would be a tangent.

Faster R-CNN RPN, anchor boxes, FPN, RoI Align, YOLO v2/v3/v5, SSD, Ultralytics. Same reasoning as 4021. Ch 22 acknowledges Faster R-CNN as historical context; deep YOLO/SSD architecture details add no value for VLM or agent readers. Web/browser agents do not need pixel-level detection.

U-Net (with VGG16 encoder), transposed convolution, Mask R-CNN, FCN heads. U-Net is the diffusion-UNet ancestor (diffusion is explicitly out of book scope) and the medical-imaging workhorse (no medical-imaging chapter exists; healthcare module 69 is LLM-focused). Ch 22.1 already lists DeepLab and Swin in the segmentation backbone table at the depth needed.

Mostly applied recipes (Detectron2, pose, crowd counting, colorization, 3D LiDAR, MMAction, Ultralytics) that are not LLM-adjacent. HOWEVER, the 3D point-cloud / LiDAR / bird's-eye-view encoding section (slides 26-37) could be a 1-sentence callout in Ch 24 (VLA Models) or Ch 67-73 (industry chapters, manufacturing/autonomous use cases). This is a weak, optional pickup, not a hard miss.

Single-agent RL refresher: MDPs, Bellman equations, policy/value iteration, SARSA, Q-learning. Standard textbook RL primer. Ch 4 (RLHF) and Ch 16 (DPO/PPO) cover the LLM-specific RL surface; classical Q-learning/SARSA pseudocode is not needed for the LLM book and the MARL conceptual carryover already landed in Ch 28.

3-slide stub introducing the Repeated-Normal-Form / MDP / Stochastic Game / POSG nested hierarchy. Pure game-theory taxonomy. Ch 28 (Multi-Agent Systems) already received the MARL conceptual carryover from 45001; this Venn diagram adds nothing actionable for an LLM-agent reader.

top_false_negatives: 4041 slides 26-37 (3D point cloud / LiDAR / bird's-eye-view encoding) - optional 1-sentence callout in Ch 24 (VLA) or industry chapters; weak pickup, not a hard miss
